The fourteen normalized digit sums are (3,2,3,2,3,4,3,2,3,4,3,4,3,6), uniquely minimized at j=2,4,8. Any zero-sum length is divisible by t. Length t would have genuine three-digit representation <q³ contradicting that digit minimum; coefficient triples of 2e attain 2t, and all optimal solutions reduce to the three cyclic rotations. The cubic inequality e<(t+1)³−1 holds for t≥4; Dirichlet gives infinitely many prime bases q≡11 mod14 (t=7u+5). Independent exact BFS for t=4,5,11,12 verifies finite shortest lengths; analytic modular orbit argument establishes the infinite family.

originality.rationale: O PASS, with a specific specialization risk. Breuer–Héthelyi–Horváth–Külshammer (Prop. 2.22, arXiv:1912.03065) already gives a general digit-sum minimization algorithm for all coprime (q,e). The 14-entry spectrum is an elementary evaluation of that method and must not be claimed as a new general algorithm. Jacob–Külshammer (arXiv:2204.09403, Conjecture 4) motivates the k=2 sharpness question but does not list the two complete progressions t≡4,5 mod7, the uniform 2t equality, or rigidity of all optimal triples. Evaluating the nontrivial parameter-uniform orbit and classifying minimizers provides a specific sharpness witness beyond an uncomputed general algorithm. Explicit caution: the prior formula may allow this computation with little extra work, and unindexed equivalent specializations could cover it.
